Upstream capacity discovery

Opt-in runtime admission discovery from authenticated local inference capacity snapshots.

About 4 min read · 3 sections

On this page
01 Configuration 02 Capacity contract 03 Verification and rollback

Enable capacityDiscovery: true on a local inference provider once. Gateway then follows its authenticated upstream capacity in memory, without rewriting gateway.json or maintaining a worker count on every Mac.

Workers: actual scheduler slots and health
  → existing router registrar: distinct healthy, registered, unfenced workers
  → authenticated GET /v1/capacity: one farm snapshot
  → existing Gateway handler: bounded refresh every 15 seconds
  → provider admission queue and availability.load.limit

Two ten-slot workers advertise twenty. Draining one lowers capacity to ten; restoring it returns to twenty. Changing a worker's actual scheduler setting changes its next observation automatically. A decrease never cancels running requests; new requests wait until the queue has room. The waiting queue stays bounded at 32 requests per provider.

Configuration

{
  "id": "local-inference",
  "type": "chat-completions-api",
  "baseUrl": "http://inference.example/v1",
  "tailnet": true,
  "credentialFile": "/private/local-inference.key",
  "capacityDiscovery": true,
  "models": { "local-workhorse": "workhorse" }
}

The opt-in is restricted to loopback or checked Tailscale inference providers. The endpoint is always {baseUrl}/capacity, with the provider's existing credential. There is no extra URL or credential to maintain. An explicit provider maxConcurrent remains a ceiling; without one, fresh discovery can exceed the gateway-wide fallback. Discovered admission is capped at 64.

Missing, invalid, stale or failed discovery restores the configured provider limit, gateway-wide limit, or default four. A complete snapshot with no slots for a configured model gives zero: new work waits until capacity returns or normal request timeout/cancellation applies. Other providers remain independent.

Numeric settings in the file stay unchanged. Older bundled app and supervisor validators that preserve unknown provider fields can keep reading this boolean while a compatible inference handler discovers capacity. Verify compatibility before activation; an older inference handler may reject the opt-in as a route change until it adopts the new code.

Admission state is shared across compatible handler generations so an update does not create another full queue budget. During a one-time upgrade from an older handler that cannot expose its counters, opted-in providers wait for that generation to finish before using a discovered budget. Active requests finish. Retired handlers stop polling and cannot reapply older configuration snapshots.

Discovery does not choose models, change routes, instructions, tools, caller permissions or queue order, or restart workers. Collection belongs to the existing inference handler. There is no new macOS background job.

Capacity contract

The read-only endpoint uses the inference bearer and returns a complete snapshot. observed_at is Unix seconds, including fractional seconds.

{
  "object": "inference_capacity",
  "version": 1,
  "complete": true,
  "observed_at": 1800000000.25,
  "models": [
    { "id": "workhorse", "max_concurrent_requests": 20 }
  ]
}

The router sums distinct healthy, registered, unfenced workers. Aliases on one worker share its scheduler. Opaque worker identities prevent counting one worker reached through several URLs. An answering worker whose capacity cannot be read makes the snapshot incomplete; incomplete snapshots cannot raise limits.

Router addresses are replicas of the same farm. Gateway takes the minimum from successful complete replicas, never their sum. A provider with several upstream models uses the minimum capacity available to any of them; missing models count as zero in a complete snapshot.

Responses are limited to 64 KiB and 128 unique model rows. Source counts must be integers from zero through 4,096. Snapshots expire after 30 seconds and cannot be more than five seconds in the future. Redirects are refused. The whole probe, including DNS and body reading, has a three-second deadline. Tailscale addresses are checked and pinned before sending the credential. Raw worker configuration, environment, requests, tool arguments and keys are never published.

Verification and rollback

gateway availability --json reports the effective local limit. Compare it with both authenticated router snapshots using the existing private credential reader; never print the key or put it in a shell argument. Drain and restore a worker and observe the limits change. Failed discovery must restore fallback.

This remains local admission, not a global reservation across Gateways. The upstream scheduler enforces actual running slots. Availability reports this Gateway's running and waiting requests; ordinary health, quota and failure precedence still applies.

Disable capacityDiscovery to return to static admission. Keep numeric settings compatible with retained older releases. A worker rollback without the endpoint safely restores static fallback. See the private deployment runbook for worker and router rollout receipts and the source of the qualified worker images.
